item.content:encoded:
I love this but there are SO many unanswered questions. This occurred in the early 21st century, and for some reason the lights have no battery backup. What?
MTF goes in with night vision goggles instead of portable lights. What?
These are relatively large animals, and the article even mentions the Foundation can implant tracking chips (in the agents), but the bugs don't have tracking devices to keep them from ambushing you out of the shadows, which is the ONLY way they hunt. What?
An audio log contains the phrase "Y-H-W-H." That's… clearly not an audio log. Did he literally say, "why-aych-double-eue-aych?" Cause that would be super weird. The tetragrammaton is unpronouncable and as such belongs in an audio log like Thursday belongs in a list of ice cream flavors.
+1 for the critters, because I love them. -1 for the writing because, what? Neutral vote.

item.content:encoded:
That probably happens in most cases, but it's not interesting to read in an article…

Containment Breach Report 363-1: MTF Eta-Seven contained the breach.
Containment Breach Report 363-2: MTF Eta-Seven contained the breach.
Containment Breach Report 363-3: MTF Eta-Seven contained the breach yet again. Man, these guys are badasses. They just contain every breach ever without any difficulty! Go them!

Not very entertaining, and rather pointless to put into an entry, right?

Now, I will say I'd like it better if at least a couple of the people from the MTF survived. ALL of them getting overpowered by the things is kinda strange, and makes the scip seem waaaay too powerful, imo. (While it's creepy as all get out, and definitely dangerous, I just don't see this one being on the level of some of the others out there for sheer "murderizing power", y'know?) Even if the survivors still called in an airstrike to level the place, having an entire specialized unit wiped out with seemingly no effort… ehh…

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I have a hard time taking the Containment Breach Log very seriously. I would imagine that SCP task forces would have the level of professionalism and efficiency that you would expect from, say, a special forces/military squad, and yet, it all just comes across really cheesy. It would be understandable that the people being attacked might be freaking out just a bit, and even so, military personnel are trained to remain calm under extreme stress. But Commander Johnson is in no such danger and therefore would probably be barking frank and clipped orders to his men. Saying things like "Good God" and Calm down Tel, for God's sake" breaks the tension and believability for me.

item.content:encoded:
Well, this entire wiki is based around "things behaving in ways they shouldn't", including but not limited to defying the laws of physics, existing, and convincing subjects that they're actually toasters; the point being that "something mundane until suddenly it's not" and "oooooo mysteeeerious" are still pretty broad categories with plenty of room for originality provided an idea is well executed.

That said, I agree with your elaboration on the genetic makeup of these things. The creepy factor of a slight mutation is (arguably) much more favorable than the cursory bit of mystery that indistinguishable genetics contributes to the article.

item.content:encoded:
For some reason this just doesn't do anything for me. I find it borderline annoying but it's a little difficult to explain why. I'll give it a try anyway because I like to be constructive with these comments.

The "something mundane until suddenly it's not" is already a tad overdone for SCPs. But it's hard to not replicate another SCP so that's not a big deal. Mentioning that they're even genetically identical to the mundane (but creepy) animal just seems to take it a bit too far into the "it's soooo mysteeeerious" place though; if there was even one small, apparently meaningless chromosome of difference or something, then that would make it both less unexplainable-for-the-sake-of-being-unexplainable, but also in its own way scarier… like any regular giant centipede is just a little genetic defect away from turning into one of these things.

And yeah, if the distorted voices were just the dying personnel praying, I think that needs to be clarified somehow, because like others I assumed these were somehow some weird Jehovah-worshiping centipedes, which was more of a "… What, really?" reaction than being creepy or scary.
